newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies to resume reform amendment voting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies to resume reform amendment voting.

text.p: Brazil's lower house of Congress would resume voting on amendments to the government's civil service reform bill later Tuesday, a government spokeswoman in Congress said.

Whips were calling government-allied lawmakers to make sure they would be in the Chamber of Deputies to vote against the amendments, most of which have been floated by the opposition in an attempt to water down the reform bill, the spokeswoman said.
Last month, the government clinched a first approval for the legislation in the Chamber of Deputies with just one vote more than the three-fifths majority needed.

It then failed to muster enough votes to kill an opposition amendment which struck down a key article of the bill. The article would have done away with jobs-for-life guarantees for newly hired public sector workers.
About seven amendments have yet to be put to votes in the lower house before the reform bill can be put to its second and final vote in the Chamber of Deputies and advance to the Senate.

The first amendment of importance likely to be voted on Tuesday seeks to prevent state and municipal governments from setting pay and pensions ceilings below a 10,800 real ($10,188) monthly cap proposed for federal workers.
The government says local governments should be given the opportunity of setting their own "sub-ceiling" at whatever level they feel most suitable to their financial situation.

Another amendment due to be voted this week aims to strike down an even more crucial article of the reform bill which would allow federal, state and municipal authorities to fire workers whose jobs are currently protected by the constitution.
Government whips say they hope to conclude voting on the amendments this week.
